The Best Restaurants In The West Village

All the spots you’ll want to know about the next time you wind up in this neighborhood full of brownstones and celebrities walking their dogs.

photo credit: Kate Previte

Bryan Kim, Will Hartman, Sonal Shah & Molly Fitzpatrick

October 20, 2026

When you walk through the West Village, you’re bound to think a few things. “This neighborhood is very charming,” for example, and “There are a lot of high-end boutiques selling $75 candles.” You’ll also see an absurd number of restaurants. Many of them are fantastic, and some just look fantastic—remember, brick walls and tiny wooden stools do not actually guarantee that the food will be any good. With that in mind, here are the West Village spots and that are absolutely worth your time. Once you’ve found a place for brunch or dinner, check out our list of the best bars in the West Village. And if you cross 6th Avenue, we've got a guide to Greenwich Village, too.

THE SPOTS

Via Carota

51 Grove St., New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Pasta

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsPrivate DiningWalk-Ins

Via Carota is always busy, and there are several reasons why. First, the Italian food is exceptional—especially the pasta, fried rabbit, and svizzerina. This restaurant also has an attractive space decorated like an Italian farmhouse, and you might see someone who’s due for their first (or next) Oscar win. Limited reservations are available 30 days out, but if you don’t snag one, you might be told to come back in several hours, so put your name on the list and get some drinks at one of the many bars within walking distance.

Find The Best Spots Nearby

Graciela

2 Bank St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Argentinian

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsSpecial OccasionsNight On The TownDinner With The ParentsImpressing Out Of TownersCorporate Cards

Everyone who works at Graciela seems personally invested in making your night a great one. At this live-fire restaurant from the team behind Argentina’s most famous steakhouse, a welcome drink appears in your hand as you walk in, and extra scoops of complimentary ice cream might materialize alongside the one you ordered. Let the sommelier pick a special bottle, and don’t leave without trying the ojo de bife, which tastes like butter sculpted into ribeye form, or the flan, one of the best we’ve ever had.

READ THE REVIEW

How to get into Graciela

Reservations are released two weeks in advance at 10am, and limited tables are available for walk-ins. For the best odds, put your name in for a seat at the bar (where, as a bonus, half portions of steak are available). On a Monday at 8:30pm, we only had to wait around 10 minutes.

9.0

Cleo

621 Hudson St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

French

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsCasual DinnersDinner With The ParentsFirst DatesBrunchSerious Takeout Operation

From the team behind Margot and Montague Diner, this rotisserie-chicken specialist is useful for a catch-up with friends that's nice but not too nice. It’s chic, with stark white walls and floral arrangements, but also pleasantly low-effort, with a menu streamlined enough that you won't spend 20 minutes deliberating over what to order. Get their baharat-marinated bird with deep-brown, warmly spiced skin. It's a great canvas for the trio of sauces, including a punchy green zhug and labne ranch.

READ THE REVIEW

How to get into Cleo

Reservations are released two weeks in advance at 10am. Cleo doesn't have a bar, but they do save room for walk-ins. We've showed up a couple of times just shortly after they open at 5pm and we've been seated right away.

8.0

Wild Cherry

38 Commerce St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

American

West Village

Perfect For:See & Be SeenFeeling HotBirthdays

Behind the lobby of the A24-run Cherry Lane Theatre, Wild Cherry is the hard-to-get-into sister restaurant of Frenchette and Le Veau d’Or (another tough reservation). Unlike its siblings, the place is only quasi-French. It looks like a disco-inclined Midwestern supper club, and, in addition to steak tartare and a croque monsieur, serves kielbasa and a lobster roll. The burger is objectively the best thing on the menu, followed closely by the cocktails and frozen custard sundae.

READ THE REVIEW

How to get into Wild Cherry

Reservations are released online two weeks in advance, but if you can’t snag one, they do take walk-ins at the bar. When we came at 4:50pm on a Wednesday, there were around eight walk-ins ahead of us in line, and we all got seated at 5pm when the restaurant opened. If it’s a weekend, get here by 4:30pm.

7.7

Semma

60 Greenwich Ave, New York, NY 10011

$$$$

Indian

West Village

Perfect For:BirthdaysDate NightsDrinking Great Cocktails

The Dhamaka team is behind Semma, which serves South Indian regional specialties typically made in rural home settings. With colorful designs on its white brick walls, and a woven bamboo ceiling, it's a pleasant place for some of the best food in the city. That is, if you can manage to get a table. Once you do, order the gunpowder dosa and a lobster tail in a turmeric-scented coconut milk sauce. We'd also recommend calling ahead to reserve the whole Dungeness crab. Only a handful are available each night.

READ THE REVIEW

How to get into Semma

Reservations are released online two weeks in advance. There aren't any tables saved for walk-ins, but there are 12 seats at the bar, so you can always try your luck there.

El Camarón Peludo

20 Cornelia St , New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Seafood

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsEating At The BarDrinking Great WineDrinks & A Light BitePeople WatchingFeeling Hot

There’s no place quite like El Camarón Peludo for eating mariscos—definitely not in NYC, possibly not the world. From the team behind Taqueria Ramirez, this romantic, lighthearted wine bar is a shrine to shrimp, with crustaceans embroidered on the curtains and printed on the glasses. Grab a seat at the lively counter for sweet red gambas carpaccio, michelada-style oysters, fried mackerel, and bright, offbeat wines. There are no reservations, but this is exactly the kind of place worth taking your chances on.

Zimmi's

72 Bedford St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

French

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsDrinking Great Wine

Stepping into this snug southern French bistro feels like entering grand-mère’s country house. The food is just as old-world homey as the sepia-lit dining room, while still refined, like artichoke soup with a chunk of foie gras. The simple yet extraordinarily flavorful pissaladière—a Niçoise tart with caramelized onions, anchovies, and black olives—is a must.

The Commerce Inn

50 Commerce St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

American

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsImpressing Out Of TownersBrunch

This Shaker-inspired tavern from the team behind Via Carota and I Sodi serves old-fashioned American food that leans very meat-and-potatoes (with lots of pickles thrown in). It’s charming, and the roast chicken is great, but you really want to come here for breakfast or brunch, when the food is less historically accurate but better overall. Book well ahead for weekend mornings, and keep an eye out for specials like a club sandwich.

Quique Crudo

27 Bedford St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

Mexican

West Village

Perfect For:Walk-InsDate Nights

Quique Crudo serves exceedingly fresh and simple Mexican seafood in a space so tiny you may accidentally eat off your neighbor’s plate. With only around 20 stools, this walk-in-only spot seems like it would be a pain to get into, but early in the night, there’s often no wait. Don’t bring a group, but do bring a date who appreciates crab tostadas and impeccable margaritas.

8.3

4 Charles Prime Rib

4 Charles Street, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

American

West Village

Perfect For:Impressing Out Of TownersLate NightsBirthdaysSpecial Occasions

Like a lot of spots on this list, 4 Charles Prime Rib is tough to get into. If you manage to score a table, prepare yourself to eat meat and drink something strong in a small dark space filled with diners who look like they talk about market caps and liquidity all day. Order a few big hunks of prime rib, and be sure to dip your fries in creamed spinach. For dessert, have a sundae, a burger (one of the best in the city), or both. If you’re looking to have dinner in a space that feels like a rich relative’s private drinking den, it doesn’t get much better than this.

READ THE REVIEW

How to get into 4 Charles Prime Rib

Reservations are released online 21 days in advance at 9am. But unless you've already eaten here, you probably won't get one. The restaurant gives preferential access to customers who are verified in the system, and the only way to get verified is to dine at 4 Charles, then ask to be put on the list. To do that, line up outside no later than 3pm, and wait until the host starts seating people around 3:45 pm. If you're one of the first few parties in line, there's a very good chance you'll get a table.

Hommali

28 7th Ave S, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Thai

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsDinner With The Parents

For a very chic date night with some pretty excellent food, check out Hommali. Perfect for your next date night, the downstairs looks like a moody library in an Architectural Digest video. And the upstairs, with its terracotta floors and a skylight the size of your average bodega, feels like dining in a palace courtyard. The food is just as stylish, with creative takes on classics: seafood cocktail with a puddle of spicy, funky tom yum instead of cocktail sauce, or vegetable fritto misto with a fermented soy and coconut sauce that echoes tom kha.

Crevette

10 Downing St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

Seafood

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsDinner With The ParentsBirthdays

Located in the former Holiday Bar space, Crevette is a bright seafood restaurant from the team behind Lord’s and Dame. Instead of English food though, a meal at Crevette is a vacation on the French Riviera—with a day trip to the Spanish coastline. Shoot oysters with coriander mignonette, snack on tuna belly on crunchy potato rosti, and finish your meal with a glorious half chicken and frites. Crevette also has a wonderful bar, so it works well for a walk-in solo dinner.

Faicco's Italian Specialities

260 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Sandwiches

West Village

Perfect For:Impressing Out Of TownersLunchSerious Takeout Operation

Faicco’s is a legendary Italian deli that you should scream about to everyone you eat lunch with regularly. It’s been around since 1900 (and has been operated by the same family throughout its entire existence), and it’s where you’ll find what we’re fairly certain is NYC’s best chicken cutlet sandwich. (It’s about the size of The Rock’s forearm.) They also have every kind of high-quality meat to stuff into a long roll. This place is more like a little grocery store than a restaurant, so grab some jarred pesto on your way out.

READ THE REVIEW

8.6

Edith's Sandwich Counter

64 Charles St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

Sandwiches

West Village

Perfect For:LunchBreakfast

All of the sandwiches at this counter-service spot take inspiration from the Jewish diaspora, like their Sephardi breakfast wrap on flaky malawach, or a chicken schnitzel club on challah. The Charles St. location is a bit bigger than the first Edith’s in Brooklyn and has the bonus of West Village charm—complete with stained glass lamps, big windows, exposed brick, and ’70s music playing through the speakers. Also, the restaurant is locked and loaded with a six-shooter slushie machine arsenal, so get an iced coffee slushie with your sandwich.

The Waverly Inn

16 Bank St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

American

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsClassic Establishment

Cozied up inside a landmark townhouse, the Waverly Inn is a modern NYC classic, known for celebrity clientele and a no-photographs policy. The American food here is solid (nothing tops the complimentary basket of biscuits), but the candlelit atmosphere is unbeatable, especially if you ensconce yourself in a red leather banquette with a view of the famous Edward Sorel mural.

The Noortwyck

289 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

American

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsSpecial OccasionsDinner With The Parents

The Noortwyck manages to get us excited about a menu that calls itself New American. Even their most basic dishes get unexpected accents, like raw oysters with seasonal garnishes like cherry and raspberry or pickled shimeji mushrooms. And despite the fact that this isn’t an Italian restaurant, their pasta is some of the best in the West Village. (That’s saying something.) The space is casual enough for after-work drinks, yet special enough for a birthday dinner. Be sure to save room for dessert.

I Sodi

314 Bleecker St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Italian

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsSpecial Occasions

I Sodi is known for two things: incredible Tuscan food that’s so simple it seems effortless, and being impossible to get into—partly because the original location was tiny. Now that the restaurant is in a larger space on Bleecker, getting a table is a bit easier, but not by much. If you're lucky enough to land a reservation, you’ll get to enjoy your choice of their house Negronis and some perfect pappardelle al limone in a faux farmhouse space with weathered floorboards. Keep in mind, the bar is saved for walk-ins, and you can get a seat there without much of a wait if you stop by early in the night.

8.5

L'Artusi

228 W 10th St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Pasta

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsEating At The Bar

There’s a correct way to do L’Artusi, and this is it: You come with one other person, and you sit at the bar. You order a crudo and the roasted mushrooms with pancetta and a fried egg, and then you share two pastas. You drink wine. You go home happy. Unlike a lot of rustic downtown Italian spots, the decor is modern with upholstered seating and gray tile floors, and a dinner here is about as good a date night as they come. You can’t go wrong with any of the pastas, and the wagyu carpaccio alone is worth coming back for.

Sappe

240 W 14th St, New York, New York 10011

$$$$

Thai

Chelsea

Perfect For:Big GroupsDrinking Great CocktailsBirthdays

This sequel to the East Village Thai spot Soothr feels like the glam afterparty of a 1970s movie premier. If you need a place that immediately sets the tone for a lively night out, stop by and eat skewers beneath a mirrored ceiling while you listen to a Thai pop soundtrack. The food—like the spicy duck laab, and a seasonal fruit salad with fish sauce—doesn’t hold back, and the elaborate cocktails keep the mood festive. Try the frozen Somsri, made with tequila, lime zest, and guava puree.

8.2

Don Angie

103 Greenwich Ave, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Italian

West Village

Perfect For:Date NightsSee & Be Seen

Instead of cacio e pepe and carbonara, Don Angie does a giant platter of rolled lasagna for two and a plate of gnocchi with provolone. Both dishes are very much worth your time, and there are some other creative pastas and little plates that belong on your table too, like a stuffed garlic flatbread and a parmesan-covered chrysanthemum salad. Eat all of those things, and you’ll realize why this is one of the top Italian restaurants in NYC. The restaurant is filled with leather and shiny things, so it’s a sleek destination for a date night. (And so is San Sabino, a seafood-centric spot from the same team, right around the corner.)

READ THE REVIEW

How to get into Don Angie

Reservations are released online seven days in advance at 9am. The bar is reserved for walk-ins, and bar seats are surprisingly attainable. Sure, you might have to wait an hour or so, but don’t be afraid to stop by and put your name in.

Buvette

42 Grove St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

French

West Village

Perfect For:BreakfastCoffee & A Light BiteDate NightsDining SoloEating At The BarLunch

Buvette is very small and consistently packed. That might not sound like a place where you want to eat a meal, but this French bistro (with locations in other cities like Paris and Tokyo) will win you over with its charm as soon as you sit down. There's a long marble bar and a big chalkboard map of France, and the homey space is filled with vintage knickknacks. Bring a date to this romantic spot for some classic French dishes like coq au vin, duck cassoulet, and escargots.

8.3

Emmett’s On Grove

39 Grove St, New York, NY 10014

$$$$
Perfect For:Casual DinnersWalk-InsBirthdays

This place—an offshoot of Emmett’s in Soho—serves exceptional thin-crust, tavern-style pies, as well as many other crowd-pleasing items like pigs in a blanket and a thick-patty burger. The room feels like a tavern from the 1970s, and nearly everything costs under $30. All of the above probably explains why the average diner is 25 years old and spiritually still in college. Though if that doesn’t describe you, don’t be deterred.

L'industrie

104 Christopher St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

Pizza

West Village

Perfect For:Impressing Out Of TownersCheap EatsCasual Dinners

L’Industrie’s original Williamsburg location has been a fixture on our best pizza list since it opened, and this second location serves the same, long-fermented sourdough pies we know and love. Each pie is topped with giant basil leaves and grated parmesan, and toppings like velvety burrata, pepperoni, or soppressata, which are all imported from Italy. Despite having more seating and donning the West Village uniform of dark wood, tin ceilings, and exposed brick walls, L’Industrie is still a casual slice shop, where orange grease drips down your wrist as you fold a piece lengthwise.

Mama's Too

325 Bleecker St, New York, New York 10014

$$$$

Pizza

West Village

Perfect For:Cheap EatsLunch

The West Village has so much good pizza, it’s unfair to other neighborhoods. Your first stop should always be L’Industrie, but after that, head to Mama’s Too. This slice shop, which started on the Upper West Side, specializes in light, crunchy square pies heavily layered with toppings like vodka sauce, whipped ricotta, and calabrian chili oil. The pepperoni and cacio e pepe are essential, and you should also try a sandwich, like the overstuffed cheesesteak or chicken alla vodka.

8.8

Sushi Katsuei

357 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10014

$$$$

Sushi

West Village

Perfect For:Dining SoloEating At The Bar

Sushi Katsuei started in Park Slope, and it became so popular that it expanded to Manhattan. This is one of the best places in the West Village to eat incredible, creative sushi for under $100. Sit at the long wooden bar, and after a couple pieces of nigiri, you’ll wonder why there aren’t more places that serve raw fish this good for this price. Omakase options start at $65 for nine pieces and a handroll, and they often include unusual options like firefly squid or barracuda.
